source.title: US too focused on Middle East and not pushing Russia hard enough, Zelensky tells BBC
source.summary: Ukraine's president voices frustration with US and says it is "strange" Trump has described Vladimir Putin as a friend.
source.evidence_text:
In an interview with the BBC at his central Kyiv office, Ukraine's president also said it was "strange" that Donald Trump had posted a picture of himself embracing Vladimir Putin as "my friend".
"It's a pity they made a focus on Middle East and they help them more… It's a pity. We have huge questions with this," Zelensky said.
Volodymyr Zelensky has voiced deep frustration with the US, saying that delays in delivering vital anti-ballistic missiles are costing Ukrainian lives and complaining that the US is not pushing Russia hard enough during peace talks.
Trump's two envoys have been trying to negotiate a peace deal between Russia and Ukraine - to end the huge loss of life. But they often seem more in tune with Moscow's position, than that of Kyiv.
The latest round of peace talks, mediated in Abu Dhabi earlier this month, made no obvious progress: "The more we know, the more problems", is how Zelensky described it.
He said talks were expected to resume in December.
Some residents have already left town for the winter and businesses closed, as power cuts and strikes on logistics networks have pushed operating costs unmanageably high.
"People can go, but we will try to defend our capital in any way. We need our capital. Without a capital, you don't have a country."
So Zelensky called for "real helpful allies, who can push Russia" to achieve results and urged the US to live up to its reputation as a strong country with "power and respect".
The US argues that it is neutral: in the complex search for a peace deal between the two sides that can hold.
But there is a "very, very big" deficit of interceptors to stop ballistic missiles and he said the Amercians were delaying deliveries of its Patriot systems.
Russian strikes across the country have been growing more frequent and more deadly: the number of civilians being killed is at an all-time high.
But he acknowledged that Ukraine was bracing for a difficult and dangerous winter.
Since a bruising encounter with Trump in the Oval Office in 2025, Zelensky has been careful how he handles relations with the United States.
But from its public statements, Russia appears to have regressed to its initial, hardline negotiating positions – on everything.
And Zelensky revealed that it was not clear whether European negotiators would be at the table, as the US envoys had announced .
Zelensky said the military here are now able to destroy about 70% of Russia's fastest drones, a statistic he said was improving.
He also confirmed that the US satellite communications system, Starlink – and its military version, Starshield – were still being restricted in occupied areas of Ukraine.
Ukrainian drone units have described their problems to the BBC, as their interceptor drones can no longer catch up with Russian Shaheds. It means those weapons then fly deeper into Ukraine, unhindered.
Ukraine's own long-range strikes against Russian targets have increased in recent weeks, including oil refineries and ships carrying weapons or fuel.
He accepted that such strikes were "very dangerous" but said Ukraine's forces "never attack" without co-ordinating with its partners.

grammar.explanation: Use “was/were expected to” followed by the base form of a verb to report what people thought would happen later. This passive structure leaves out who held the expectation. It reports an expectation, so it does not confirm that the event happened.
grammar.example_quote: The talks were expected to resume in December, according to Zelensky.

quiz.question: What is the main concern Zelensky expresses in the reading?
options: The US is not doing enough to help Ukraine and pressure Russia.
The US is putting too much pressure on Russia.
The US has stopped seeking a peace agreement.
option_feedback: Correct. He criticises delays in military support and wants more pressure on Russia.
He wants the US to increase pressure on Russia.
The reading says the US is seeking an agreement that can last.

quiz.question: What comparison does Zelensky make about US support?
options: He says Ukraine receives more help than the Middle East.
He says the US provides more help to the Middle East.
He says the US provides equal help to both.
option_feedback: This reverses his complaint about where the US provides more help.
Correct. He complains that the US focuses on the Middle East and helps it more.

quiz.question: What result does the reading report from the latest negotiations in Abu Dhabi?

quiz.question: How does the US description of its role differ from Zelensky's request?
options: The US describes itself as neutral, while Zelensky wants it to pressure Russia.
The US wants more pressure on Russia, while Zelensky asks it to remain neutral.
Both say the US should avoid trying to reach an agreement.

This reverses the positions described in the reading.

quiz.question: What does “shortage” mean in the report about defensive missiles?
options: There are more missiles than Ukraine needs.
There are fewer missiles than Ukraine needs.
The missiles are no longer needed.
option_feedback: A “shortage” means there is too little of something, not too much.
Correct. The available supply does not meet the need.

quiz.question: Which reason for some businesses shutting is supported by the reading?

Businesses were waiting for the December talks.
Power cuts and attacks made running businesses too expensive.
option_feedback: The reading does not connect business closures to a requirement from negotiations.

quiz.question: What does “resume” tell us about the talks expected in December?

They would take place for the first time.
They would certainly produce an agreement.
option_feedback: Correct. “Resume” means to continue an activity after a pause.
“Resume” refers to an activity that has already begun.
“Resume” describes continuing, without promising a successful result.

quiz.question: What does “were expected to resume” establish about the December talks?
options: They had already taken place.
People thought they would continue, but this wording does not confirm they did.
They could not take place.
option_feedback: The structure reports an expectation about a later event, not a completed event.
Correct. An expectation is different from confirmation that something happened.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly uses “was expected to” to describe an expectation about a delivery?
options: The delivery was expected arrive on Friday.
The delivery expected to arrive on Friday.
The delivery was expected to arrive on Friday.
option_feedback: The pattern needs “to” before the base form “arrive”.
The passive reporting pattern needs “was” before “expected”.
Correct. “Was expected to” is followed by the base form “arrive”.

vocabulary.definition: Broadly aligned with someone's views or priorities, without necessarily having a formal agreement.
Conducted with a third party helping opposing sides seek an agreement.
Returned to an earlier, less constructive position after apparent movement away from it.
Unwilling to soften demands or make substantial compromises.
Participating directly in discussions where decisions or agreements are being negotiated.

grammar.explanation: Use “while” followed by an “-ing” form to acknowledge a contrasting consideration without making it a cause. The understood subject must match the main-clause subject; here, Zelensky acknowledges danger while asserting coordination with partners.
grammar.example_quote: While acknowledging that such strikes were highly dangerous, Zelensky said Ukrainian forces never conducted them without coordinating with partners.

quiz.question: Which statement best captures the central tension in the report?
options: Zelensky wants stronger US pressure and military support, while the US presents itself as a neutral mediator.
Zelensky wants the US to withdraw from diplomacy so that Ukraine can negotiate without outside involvement.
The US and Ukraine agree that defensive missile deliveries should await a completed peace agreement.
option_feedback: Correct: the reading contrasts Zelensky's demands for pressure and defensive support with the US explanation of its neutrality.
The reading reports criticism of US conduct, but no demand that the US withdraw from diplomacy.
The reading describes urgent criticism of delivery delays, not agreement to postpone deliveries until peace is secured.

quiz.question: What does the assessment that the US envoys appear more “in tune with” Moscow imply?
options: They have formally accepted every Russian demand.
Their apparent outlook is closer to Moscow's position than Kyiv's.
They have ended their efforts to reach an agreement.
option_feedback: “In tune with” suggests alignment of outlook; it does not establish formal acceptance of every demand.
Correct: the phrase describes apparent similarity in views or priorities, while preserving uncertainty.
The reading still describes the envoys as seeking a peace deal.

quiz.question: What does “regressed” contribute to the description of Russia's negotiating stance?
options: It indicates that Russia has offered a substantially new compromise.
It establishes that Russia has formally withdrawn from all discussions.
It suggests a return to earlier, less flexible demands.
option_feedback: A new compromise would suggest movement towards agreement, whereas “regressed” signals movement backwards.
Returning to earlier positions does not establish withdrawal from discussions.
Correct: “regressed” presents the apparent return to initial hardline positions as a setback.

quiz.question: What remains uncertain when Zelensky questions whether Europeans will be “at the table”?
options: Whether European negotiators will participate directly.
Whether European negotiators have already endorsed the final agreement.
Whether European negotiators have rejected mediation as a principle.
option_feedback: Correct: “at the table” concerns direct participation in the talks.
Participation and endorsement are different matters, and the reading describes no final agreement.
The uncertainty concerns participation, not a stated rejection of mediation.

quiz.question: Which account accurately preserves the scope of Zelensky's statement about Starlink and Starshield?
options: Restrictions on both systems had been lifted throughout occupied Ukrainian territory.
Both systems remained restricted in occupied Ukrainian territory.
Both systems were entirely unavailable throughout Ukraine.
option_feedback: The reading says the restrictions remained; it does not report that they had been lifted.
Correct: this retains both the continuing restrictions and the geographical scope of the statement.
Restrictions in occupied territory do not establish complete unavailability throughout the country.

quiz.question: Which interpretation preserves the scope of Zelensky's reported 70% figure?
options: Ukraine destroys approximately 70% of all incoming Russian weapons.
Ukraine destroys approximately 70% of incoming ballistic missiles.
Ukraine can destroy approximately 70% of Russia's fastest drones.
option_feedback: The reported figure concerns a particular category of drones, not all weapons.
The reading distinguishes the drone figure from the deficit of missiles used against ballistic attacks.
Correct: this retains both the approximate figure and the specific category to which it applies.

quiz.question: In the passage about defensive missiles, what does “deficit” identify?
options: The amount by which the available interceptors fall short of requirements.
The total number of interceptors currently available for use.
The number of interceptors already used against incoming missiles.
option_feedback: Correct: “deficit” identifies the shortfall between available supply and requirements.
The available stock is one side of the comparison; “deficit” names the amount missing.
“Deficit” describes an unmet requirement, not the quantity already used.

quiz.question: What can be inferred from the report that some Russian drones travelled farther “unhindered”?
options: Russian drones no longer encounter any Ukrainian resistance anywhere.
Those drones continued because the interceptor drones described could not catch them.
Ukraine had deliberately stopped attempting to intercept Russian drones.
option_feedback: “Unhindered” describes the progress of the drones discussed; it does not justify a claim about every location.
Correct: the reading connects their continued progress with interceptor drones being unable to catch them.
An inability to catch particular drones does not establish a decision to stop interception attempts.

quiz.question: Which distinction does Zelensky's statement about coordination preserve?
options: Coordination with partners proves that the strikes carry no danger.
Acknowledging danger means that Ukraine has suspended such strikes.
He acknowledges the danger while maintaining that such strikes are coordinated with partners.
option_feedback: The reading presents coordination and danger together; coordination does not eliminate the acknowledged risk.
The reading contains no claim that acknowledging danger led to a suspension.
Correct: his account combines an admission of risk with a claim about how the strikes are conducted.

quiz.question: Which interpretation of the business closures is supported by the reading?
options: Electricity and logistics disruption had raised operating costs beyond what affected businesses could manage.
Businesses closed as a precaution against expected winter disruption while their current costs remained manageable.
The closures show that electricity and logistics disruption had forced every business in the town to stop trading.
option_feedback: Correct: the reading links closures to disruption that had already made operating costs unmanageably high.
This shifts the explanation from existing financial pressure to anticipated disruption and contradicts the description of costs.
The reading reports business closures without stating that every business had closed.

quiz.question: Which rewrite preserves the concessive meaning and understood subject of the clause beginning “While acknowledging”?
options: Because he acknowledged that the strikes were dangerous, Zelensky said his forces never conducted them without coordinating with partners.
Although he acknowledged that the strikes were dangerous, Zelensky said his forces never conducted them without coordinating with partners.
Until he acknowledged that the strikes were dangerous, Zelensky said his forces never conducted them without coordinating with partners.
option_feedback: “Because” introduces a reason; the original clause acknowledges a contrasting consideration without establishing that causal link.
Correct: “although” makes the concession explicit, and “he” refers to Zelensky, the subject of the main clause.
“Until” introduces a time boundary that the original concessive clause does not express.

quiz.question: What does “bracing for” reveal about Zelensky's description of the coming winter?
options: He regards the difficult period as already over.
He guarantees a particular outcome for Ukraine's defence.
Ukraine anticipates difficulty and is preparing for it.
option_feedback: “Bracing for” points towards an anticipated challenge, not a completed one.
The expression conveys preparation and expectation, not certainty about a specific outcome.
Correct: the phrase combines anticipation of hardship with preparation to face it.
